extracted.intended_audience: NLP/ML researchers, meta-science community, and practitioners building computational tools for analyzing peer reviews (area chairs, reviewers, and annotation teams working on peer-review quality)
extracted.subtask_description: Annotating and computationally analyzing peer-review text across four layers (paper sections, aspect categories, statement purpose, and statement significance) for ML/NLP conference reviews (ICLR-focused dataset) and defining evaluation tasks for peer-review quality estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology (Layer 1: Paper Section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology is the section reviewers comment on most frequently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers focus heavily on methodology; many major and minor comments relate to methodological concerns. Empirical and theoretical soundness are often judged against the Methodology section. When annotating, expect high prevalence of labels tied to Methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments (Layer 1: Paper Section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments are the second most-commented section after Methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers comment on experimental design and results; important for assessing empirical soundness and meaningful comparisons. Questions and criticisms often target Experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Work (Layer 1: Paper Section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Related Work is a frequently-commented section, often tied to novelty and meaningful comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers use Related Work to assess novelty and to compare the current work to prior literature; lack of citations or poor comparisons are common criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem Definition / Idea (PDI) (Layer 1: Paper Section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem definition or the core idea of the paper; reviewers comment on its clarity and interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDI tends to garner positive attention at high-quality venues (authors usually submit good problem definitions), and reviewers sometimes appreciate PDI; when criticized it may influence novelty/impact judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results (Layer 1: Paper Section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Results section where outcomes, metrics, and reported findings are presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers discuss Results in relation to experiments and methodology; results co-occur with assessments of empirical soundness and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall paper (OAL) (Layer 1: Paper Section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic comments about the paper as a whole; includes overall assessments and high-level recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often used when reviewers judge appropriateness to venue or provide their recommendation; summary or general feedback may be annotated as OAL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets / Data Description (Layer 1: Paper Section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments related to datasets used, data collection, and data description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotations on data often co-occur with empirical soundness, experiments, and analysis concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction / Abstract / ABS / INT (Layer 1: Paper Section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introductory material including abstract and introduction (annotators sometimes label brief summaries as INT/ABS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers often begin with a concise summary of the paper; such summary text may be annotated as INT or ABS and can overlap with overall comments (OAL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis (Layer 1: Paper Section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical sections where authors interpret results, perform ablations, error analysis, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers critique the depth and correctness of analysis; deficits here relate to empirical/theoretical soundness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables/Figures (Layer 1: Paper Section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Visualizations and tabular representations in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation and formatting concerns often target Tables/Figures; questions frequently refer to these elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography (Layer 1: Paper Section)
rubrics_metrics.description: References and cited prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers tend to be neutral when commenting on bibliography; bibliography comments often co-occur with meaningful comparisons and related work critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future Work / External Information / Abstract (Layer 1: Paper Section - lower attention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Future work, external information, and abstract receive significantly fewer comments from reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sections are less frequently discussed; reviewers rarely comment extensively on Future Work or External Information in ICLR reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical/Theoretical Soundness (EMP) (Layer 2: Aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the work is empirically and/or theoretically sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary aspect reviewers focus on; highly judged against Methodology, Experiments, Results, Related Work, Problem Definition, Data, and Analysis. Significance labels (major/minor) often concern EMP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful Comparisons (CMP) (Layer 2: Aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the paper makes meaningful comparisons with prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates most to Related Work, Methodology, Experiments, and Results. Bibliography may be highlighted to support comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance / Volume of Work (SUB) (Layer 2: Aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amount and depth of technical contribution or experimental substance in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often critiqued; deficits in substance attract criticism and suggestions on how to increase the volume/quality of contribution to warrant publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (CLA) (Layer 2: Aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity of writing, composition, and overall understandability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity is appreciated when present and attracts negative comments when lacking; inter-dependent with Methodology and Empirical/Theoretical Soundness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and Formatting (Layer 2: Aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of figures, tables, layout, and general formatting/presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mostly produces minor comments; heavily associated with Tables/Figures and overall paper presentation issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact (IMP) (Layer 2: Aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential future impact of the work on the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers discuss impact in relation to Methodology, Related Work, Experiments, and Results; often considered when judging significance and recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (NOV) (Layer 2: Aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Newness or originality of the contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty may be implicit and is sometimes low in explicit mention; reviewers often gauge novelty via Methodology and Related Work comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation (REC) (Layer 2: Aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer's stance or suggested decision about acceptance/rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers often place recommendation scores in a dedicated field and rarely state explicit recommendation in review text; when present, it usually pertains to the overall paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness / Within-scope (Layer 2: Aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the submission is appropriate for the venue / within scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low attention at ICLR (top-tier venue) because submissions are typically within scope; comments about appropriateness appear less frequently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary (SMY) (Layer 3: Purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer statement that summarizes the paper (often at the start of a review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonly present in reviews; summarization statements indicate reviewer understanding and are often neutral in sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestion (Layer 3: Purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer proposes improvements or changes to the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions are comparatively more common in accepted paper reviews; suggestions often target Methodology, Experiments, and Related Work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deficit (Layer 3: Purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer highlights a weakness or shortcoming in the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deficits occur more in rejected paper reviews and are commonly associated with Methodology, Related Work, Experiments, and Analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appreciation (APC) (Layer 3: Purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive statements praising aspects of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appreciation appears more in accepted paper reviews; often linked to Methodology, Experiments, Results, and Problem Definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion (DIS) (Layer 3: Purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer brings understanding, knowledge, or context; objective, neutral commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussions are typically neutral and appear across Methodology, Related Work, Experiments, and Results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question (QSN) (Layer 3: Purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer poses questions to authors seeking clarification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximately 10% of review comments are questions; questions often highlight deficits and appear on Methodology, Experiments, Tables/Figures, and Related Work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism (CRT) (Layer 3: Purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit critical evaluation or negative judgment of parts of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A major category in reviews; more prevalent in rejected paper reviews; critical comments often determine major significance and map to Methodology, Experiments, Results, and Related Work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback (Layer 3: Purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer-provided commentary intended to inform authors (overlaps with recommendation but present as textual feedback).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less frequently used as reviewers usually use the recommendation field for explicit fate suggestions; textual feedback can be present but is rare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance: Major / Minor / General (Layer 4: Significance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each review statement is labeled by its significance: major comment, minor comment, or general comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major comments often contain decisive Criticism or Appreciation relevant to acceptance/rejection. Minor comments discuss points, raise questions, point out deficits, or provide suggestions. General comments commonly summarize work or provide non-opinionated discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment Labels (Positive / Negative / Neutral)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentiment annotation of review statements across layers: NEU, POS, NEG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most review texts are neutral, but POS and NEG are present; EMP, EXP, OAL, RES, NOV, REC, IMP have higher positive instances for accepted papers and higher negative for rejected papers. Sentiment can be layer- and label-specific and may help infer paper fate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-label nature of labeling (annotation principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: A review statement can correspond to multiple paper sections and multiple aspects (multi-label classification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotation and downstream models should allow multi-label assignments; some textual units should be duplicated in training as many-label instances are converted to multiple single-label instances for some baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation procedure and quality standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for annotators: use technical-background annotators, read entire review first, annotate by selecting text spans (typically sentences), resolve confusions in team meetings, two-month training exercise, ~40 minutes average per review annotation time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff's Alpha) reported as: Layer1=0.86, Layer2=0.70, Layer3=0.73, Layer4=0.84. Use these practices to ensure annotation consistency and to report IAA for dataset quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task 1: Review–paper section correspondence (computational task requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a peer review text, identify which paper section(s) it corresponds to (multi-label).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat as multi-label sentence classification; include general sections listed in Table 2. Provide label-wise micro-averaged F1 scores as evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task 2: Aspect-category detection (computational task requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a peer review text, identify the aspect(s) of the paper being commented on (multi-label).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aspects follow Layer 2 labels; allied subtask: sentiment detection per aspect/section. Use multi-label classification and report micro-averaged F1 scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task 3: Review-statement purpose detection (computational task requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a peer review statement, identify the role/purpose: Summary, Suggestion, Deficit, Appreciation, Discussion, Question, Criticism, or Feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps infer reviewer intent; treat as sentence-level classification and report label-wise F1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task 4: Review-statement significance detection (computational task requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a peer review statement, identify the statement's significance: major, minor, or general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentence-level classification; report F1 scores and consider how major/minor mapping correlates with other layers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task 5: Peer-review summarization and meta-review generation (computational task requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate concise summaries of reviews (per-review and combined across reviewers) and attempt automatic meta-review generation (including recommendation and justification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarization can be extractive or abstractive; evaluate with ROUGE (R1, R2, R-L) and precision/recall. Meta-review generation should include: a concise description of submission content, a concise summary of reviewer discussion, and an explicit recommendation with justification (per ICLR metareview guide). This is a challenging NLG task requiring summarization, redundancy elimination, diversity estimation, and sentiment analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline modeling & feature guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Baseline representations and modeling choices used for Tasks 1–4: TF-IDF (with context as previous+next sentences), Universal Sentence Encoder (USE, DAN version), hand-crafted features (HCF), and BERT-based sequential sentence classification (BERT-SSC and BERT+Transformer+CRF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hand-crafted features include: # of nouns, # of adjectives, exclamation presence, numeric presence, % presence, date presence, # of mathematical terms, # of adverbs, sentence length, # of verbs, label-specific frequent terms, presence of wh-question words, presence of '?' character. Use sequential sentence classification to capture context. Classical classifiers tried include SVM, MultinomialNB, Decision Trees, SGD; Random Forest performed best among traditional classifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation protocol standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended evaluation procedures for baselines: 80%:20% train-test split, random oversampling of minority labels to address class imbalance, report label-wise micro-averaged F1 scores, and overall accuracy figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BERT-based baselines (pre-trained on scientific data such as SciBERT) and context-aware variants outperform traditional baselines. For summarization, report ROUGE scores and use both extractive (TextRank) and abstractive (Transformer) baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data & domain scope guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset is based on ICLR (ML/NLP conference) peer reviews and thus reflects a domain-specific distribution of reviewer attention and label prevalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect higher frequency of EMP/Methodology/Experiments labels and lower explicit mentions of novelty or appropriateness; caution when generalizing to non-ML/STEM domains—labels and distributions may differ and ontologies might need adaptation.
